title: Resolve requirements by strict direct identifiers
objective: Define the strict sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1 format <work-item-id>_REQ_<###>, confirm that authoritative requirements are declared only by work-item.json, register the identifier for direct reference validation, and resolve bare requirement identifiers through the local repository scope with sdlc ref resolve --ref.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository uses main for active work and the existing master release ref remains the release boundary.

request.text:
Requirement references are plan strings following their own syntax but they're not directly resolvable. We need to explicitly support references as directly resolvable identifiers. If we don't already have a requirement identififer schema/format, we need to implement one, sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1 using th efollowing format: <work-item-id>_REQ_<###>. Requirements are _only_ declared via work-item.json [this needs to be confirmed by reviewing all schemas and ensuring requirements are only declared in work-item.json documents]. Once we have a strict sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1 we can support repository local calls, sdlc ref resolve --ref <sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1> from within the repository's scope.

Prepare a .docs/work-items/* and commit the work item.

scope.name: requirement-authority-audit
scope.description: Audit every repository schema and existing work-item/task artifact to distinguish authoritative requirement declarations in work-item.json from derived requirement references, projections, and coverage mappings.
scope.reason: Direct resolution must have one unambiguous declaration source and must not accidentally resolve derived assessment or test-strategy records as requirements.

scope.name: requirement-identifier-schema
scope.description: Add the marked standalone sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1 string schema for the strict <work-item-id>_REQ_<###> identifier form.
scope.reason: The dynamic reference registry requires a versioned schema before the identifier can be directly validated.

scope.name: local-requirement-resolution
scope.description: Extend repository-local reference resolution so a bare requirement identifier resolves to its matching requirements.items object in .docs/work-items/<work-item-id>/work-item.json.
scope.reason: Agents need a direct sdlc ref resolve --ref <requirement-identifier> command without constructing a work-item file selector.

scope.name: compatibility-and-errors
scope.description: Preserve existing qualified requirement selectors and provide deterministic non-zero reports for malformed, missing, duplicate, or out-of-scope requirement identifiers without writes.
scope.reason: The new shorthand must be additive and safe for existing references and agent remediation workflows.

scope.name: validation-evidence
scope.description: Add dynamic registry, authority-boundary, direct-resolution, nested-repository, failure, and read-only regression coverage plus the complete repository test gate.
scope.reason: The feature changes both syntax registration and semantic resolution and needs evidence for each boundary.

nonGoals.name: global-requirement-resolution
nonGoals.description: Do not implement global sdlc://repo requirement resolution or remote repository lookup.
nonGoals.reason: The request is explicitly limited to repository-local resolution from within the repository scope.

nonGoals.name: derived-requirement-authority
nonGoals.description: Do not treat work-item-assessment, work-item-requirements projections, test-strategy requirements, or task-local requirement lists as authoritative declaration sources.
nonGoals.reason: Requirements are declared by work-item.json for this local resolver; derived records remain references, assessments, or coverage projections.

nonGoals.name: reference-migration
nonGoals.description: Do not rewrite existing qualified work-item requirement references or migrate historical task records as part of adding the shorthand.
nonGoals.reason: The direct identifier is additive and existing qualified references must remain compatible.

nonGoals.name: requirement-lifecycle
nonGoals.description: Do not approve, edit, normalize, or otherwise mutate requirement declarations during validation or resolution.
nonGoals.reason: Resolution is read-only lookup and does not change work-item lifecycle or content.

items.name: requirement-authority
items.description: Authoritative requirement declarations for the local resolver must exist only in work-item.json requirements.items; other schema/artifact fields named requirements may contain derived projections, references, assessments, or coverage but are not declaration sources.
items.reason: A direct identifier must resolve deterministically to one authoritative record.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An audit of every local schema and all existing .docs/work-items artifacts records work-item.json requirements.items as the only authoritative declaration location and identifies all other requirement-bearing fields as non-authoritative.

Resolver tests prove a matching identifier is selected from the target work-item.json requirements.items and is not sourced from assessment, normalized projection, task strategy, or task payload records.

items.name: strict-requirement-identifier
items.description: The repository must persist and register sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1 as a standalone string schema whose canonical form is <work-item-id>_REQ_<###>, with an uppercase prefix, numeric work-item component, literal _REQ_, and exactly three decimal digits.
items.reason: Direct validation requires one strict, versioned identifier contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The schema has $id https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/requirement-identifier/v1, type string, x-sdlc-reference-type true, the exact canonical pattern, and valid root examples.

Dynamic sdlc ref validate accepts valid requirement identifiers and rejects malformed prefixes, separators, missing digits, non-numeric digits, extra digits, and qualified selector forms when supplied as the bare identifier type.

items.name: local-requirement-resolution
items.description: sdlc ref resolve --ref <requirement-identifier> must resolve a valid bare identifier from any nested current-repository directory to the matching requirement object in .docs/work-items/<work-item-id>/work-item.json.
items.reason: Agents need a direct local lookup that returns the requirement data and source document rather than only syntactic validation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Resolving WI-0023_REQ_001 from the repository root and a nested repository directory returns valid=true, repositoryPath .docs/work-items/WI-0023/work-item.json, format json, and the matching requirement object.
The returned requirement object includes the requested identifier and its complete name, description, reason, and acceptanceCriteria fields without mutation.

items.name: resolution-errors-and-compatibility
items.description: Direct requirement resolution must report deterministic non-zero failures for unknown work items, missing requirement IDs, duplicate requirement IDs, malformed IDs, and identifiers outside the operative repository, while preserving existing qualified requirement selector resolution.
items.reason: Shorthand resolution must be safe, diagnosable, and backward-compatible.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Missing, malformed, duplicate, or out-of-scope requirement references return valid=false or a non-zero CLI result with actionable findings and no file writes.
Existing WI-0007#work-item.json#requirement/WI-0007_REQ_001 resolution remains passing and returns the same requirement data shape.

items.name: test-and-schema-gate
items.description: The implementation and validation tasks must record dynamic reference-schema, authority-audit, direct-resolution, failure, compatibility, read-only, typecheck, build, and full-test evidence before their task commits.
items.reason: The feature spans schema discovery, local filesystem lookup, CLI behavior, and repository invariants.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The complete repository test suite, schema audit, and sdlc work-item validate --work-item WI-0023 command pass before the work-item commit.
